narrative.summaryIntro:
Konark Sun Temple, located in Odisha, is one of the most remarkable architectural achievements of medieval India and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I during the Eastern Ganga dynasty, the temple is dedicated to Surya (the Sun God). The entire temple is designed in the shape of a massive stone chariot with twelve wheels, each representing the twelve months of the solar year.

The temple is renowned for its intricate stone carvings, astronomical symbolism, and innovative architectural design. The walls are adorned with elaborate sculptures depicting various themes from Hindu mythology, celestial bodies, and daily life scenes. Though partially ruined, the temple remains a testament to the architectural brilliance and artistic sophistication of medieval Indian civilization. The temple's unique design and historical significance make it one of India's most important heritage sites.
